AI and your engineering tools

How to connect AI to CAD software

To connect AI-assisted work to CAD software, first confirm that the installed app and connector support your host and build. Then select the document and context, review the proposed task and approve only the native action you intend. A website preview is not that connection.

Work through the connection checkpoints.

  1. Check connector status.

    Use the software directory to distinguish available beta tools from integrations in development and upcoming discovery entries. A product listing is not proof of a working connection.

    Check software availability

  2. Request the right Windows beta build.

    Ask for access, exact build requirements and host compatibility. Follow the supplied installation instructions. No qualified public installer is currently offered on the website.

    Read installation guidance

  3. Select the supported host and document.

    Open the intended engineering application and identify its document through the connection flow supplied with your build. Installed software and a connected document are different checkpoints.

    Read connection guidance

  4. Provide bounded context.

    Select the objects or relevant context you want reviewed. State units, target dimensions and retained relationships. Do not assume the model can see every open document or local file.

    Review selected context

  5. Separate explanation, planning and action.

    Start with Ask or Plan to make intent clear. For a supported Build, inspect the proposed scope and exact approval before changing the native document.

    Understand task modes

  6. Verify the outcome before continuing.

    Check host readback and the intended result. Preserve an uncertain operation reference and reconcile it before repeating a change. A successful reply is not engineering acceptance.

    Review native approval

These checkpoints describe the connection and review process. They do not promise a provider or model integration, universal CAD conversion, or support for every operation in a listed host. Website demonstrations remain scripted.
